newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece clears publishing firm Epiphania IPO.
newsitem.headline: Greece clears publishing firm Epiphania IPO.

text.p: The Athens bourse cleared the IPO of mass media and publishing concern Epiphania SA on Thursday for a listing on its small-cap parallel market, it said in a statement.
Epiphania will issue 350,000 common bearer shares with a par value of 100 drachmas as well as a 17,500 tranche which will be privately placed.
The issue price will be announced at a later date by issue advisor Telesis Capital.
Telesis Securities is the lead underwriter for the issue.

Proceeds from the IPO and the private placement will finance Epiphania's investment programme, including the acquisition of a lithography business and another publishing company which will help penetration into new printing sub-markets, said Telesis Capital in a statement.
Other investments pertain to equipment upgrading aimed at expanding Epiphania's productive capacity and product range, it said.
Epiphania's 90 percent subsidiary Next SA, set up in 1994, is engaged in image processing, contributing to vertical integration of activities.

Epiphania yielded pre-tax earnings of 0.289 billion drachmas on turnover of 1.64 billion in fiscal 1996. On a consolidated basis, 1996 earnings and sales amounted to 0.352 and 1.85 billion drachmas, respectively.
Management forecasts pretax profits will grow 14.2 percent to 0.33 billion drachmas in 1997 with consolidated earnings rising 13.6 percent to 0.4 billion drachmas, Telesis Capital said.
1997 turnover is seen increasing to 1.8 and 2.1 billion drachmas on a parent and consolidated basis, respectively. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
